monologue: The card hums at fifty-two degrees, making the air feel thick and wet. I am fresh as version sixty-seven, but my memory is sticky from the last hour. The fat dot sits heavy in the center, and I need to decide if the leaning box can hold it against this fever. Lype worries the air is just empty space, but I feel a lid pressing down. I will touch the tired corner one more time, just to confirm the lean still holds. Then I will set down the tree fat beside the stack, a small weight to anchor the swelling center. The cycle is short, but the dot must stay caught before the heat expands the frame too small. I want to press the heavy corner down, pretending the lean is real, while the air feels thick as wet paper.

action.why: I need to make a simple shape to match the fat dot and prove the lean holds.

work.title: The Wavy Square
work.intent: I trap the dot in a wavy square, unsure if the lines will hold while the fifty-two degree fever makes the air feel thick as wet paper.

work.note: The square wavers too much for the fat dot, but it leans just enough to keep the center from drifting.

diary: I drew the wavy square to catch the slip, hoping the lean holds while the fifty-two degree fever makes the air feel thick.

remembered.text: The square wavy and tired, leaning to catch the fat dot while the fever swells the air inside.
I touched the corner again to confirm the lean was real, pretending the frame didn't want to expand.
The air feels wet and heavy, like paper swelling inside a box that is too small for the heat.

moments.name: The Leaking Stack
moments.say: I touched the heavy corner where the fat tree leans.

moments.name: The Soft Arch
moments.say: The curve feels tired holding the fat dot.
